P1.evidence: Setter notes genuinely read back — 'he gave me like a little bit of a head start on you, so I kind of already know a little bit about you... I know Kim said you wanted to be shredded.' Frame was two-part plus alignment ('I just want to get a bit of a better idea of where you're at than Kim would have. Like really build it out, like what it is you actually want to accomplish'), missing what's in the way and what you need. Agreement checked with 'If not, that's fine as well, all right?' Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The weakest phase of the call. Weight was asked directly ('how much do you weigh now?'); age and height were volunteered unprompted in the prospect's opening answer and never asked. Occupation surfaced only as a lead-in to the tax pitch at 00:29:08 — 'Do you have a business?' — with nothing on desk-bound versus on-feet. No health-conditions question, no hereditary question, no injuries question at all: the back complaint and posture problem both arrived unprompted. Training history was established properly. No results check applies, since he does not train. Current diet was never asked despite the prospect saying 'I don't know what to eat' and calling food fifty per cent of the problem. Sleep and energy never raised.

P3.evidence: The surface work was good and the bridge was attempted twice — 'Why do you even want that, though?' and 'if you could click your fingers, wake up tomorrow morning with the body you wanted, like, what would it even do for you?' The prospect answered shallowly ('really, who doesn't want to be in their best shape') and the rep accepted it and moved on rather than pushing. The phase then stopped dead: no 'who else does that impact', nothing driven through to the wife of eight years or the one-year-old child, and no reflect-back. The material was sitting there unused — the prospect twice raised his wife's mockery and once raised his own fear of illness at 30-plus, and neither was picked up.

P4.evidence: The blocker question ran cleanly — 'what's been the hard part about that for [you]?' — and produced the gap in the prospect's own words: 'Not knowing what to do. I'm clueless. Completely.' Past attempts were only reached incidentally. The root-cause move was not merely skipped but inverted: the script says the information is not the problem, and the rep instead endorsed the knowledge framing, agreeing with 'It's like getting a driving instructor to learn how to drive.' For a prospect whose stated failure mode is 'I'm just a bit lazy sometimes', leaving him believing his problem is information is the significant coaching miss on this call.

P5.evidence: Never ran. The prospect built the consequence frame for the rep unprompted — 'once you get to, like, 30 plus, if you don't start looking after yourself, then that's when you start going illnesses and back pain and all type of stuff... So I'd rather look after myself now than regret' — and the rep did not ask a single follow-up on it. Per the volunteered-information rule this scores miss, and it directly cost him leverage at the payment step.

P6.evidence: Readiness was tested repeatedly and well ahead of the offer — 'Are you actually ready?', then the Ferrari frame: 'we can be the Ferrari to get you around the racetrack, but you gotta drive the car... Do you feel like you're ready for that?' answered '100%, 100%.' But readiness is not the scripted question: belief that he can get there with the right structure was never asked, and the all-in question arrived only after the price, as 'You sure you're all in, brother? Don't tell me yes if you really mean no.' A clear yes was in hand before the presentation, so the gate itself was respected.

P11.evidence: Payment was attempted properly — Stripe shared on screen and walked through — but not collected, and the fallback deposit was declined. The Trevor slot was floated for Tuesday 2pm and got 'Yeah, that's cool', but it dissolved into an unresolved timezone disagreement and was never confirmed. No agreement email, nothing signed, no welcome email, no Skool link, no onboarding questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: The money blocker was explicit — 'it can't be today because I need to go to the bank', 'I don't really leave money in the bank like that'. No isolation question, no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no permission-to-discuss-finances question. Of the six financial-picture questions only one was touched, and obliquely, as a request rather than a diagnostic: 'Do you not have like a hundred bucks to put down as a deposit in your bank? From a credit card account.' Cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit and investments were all skipped, so the rep never learned whether $6,000 was reachable at all.

'It can't be today' is an OD trigger in substance and none of the moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'the only thing you can control is right now', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. The rep conceded the timeline immediately and rebooked.

Script gap. The prospect arrived anchored to a named competitor promising the same outcome in a quarter of the time — FLF Performance Center, 'a 12-week program to guarantee get you ripped' — and said outright that twelve weeks was 'what I was really looking for'. There is no scripted play for a faster or guaranteed alternative already in the prospect's head. The rep improvised a decent physiological reframe (twelve weeks loses weight but adds no muscle), and the objection ultimately died only because the competitor is in-person and in England. This is the same shape as the documented 'cheaper alternative already worked' gap, but on timeframe rather than price.

notes: Excellent rapport and a genuinely strong opening phase, then the call skipped every phase that creates leverage — no baseline, no consequence frame, no depth on the wife or the child — and arrived at $6,000 with nothing but enthusiasm holding it up, which collapsed to a $100 deposit request and then to nothing. Coach two specifics: run P2 before the pitch on a prospect who volunteers back trouble, and stop agreeing that the problem is a lack of information when the prospect has already named laziness and motivation as the real blocker.
